properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, north winds 20 to 30 kt
with gusts to 35 kt and very steep and hazardous seas 8 to 12
ft due to a mix of wind seas and building swell at 11 seconds
expected. For the Small Craft Advisory, north winds 15 to 25
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and steep seas 7 to 9 ft due to a
mix of wind seas and building swell at 11 seconds expected.

* WHERE...Small craft advisory conditions will affect all the
area Saturday afternoon. Then, late Saturday afternoon through
early Sunday morning, Hazardous Seas Warning conditions will
affect areas south of Port Orford beyond 5 nm from shore with
Small Craft Advisory elsewhere. Small craft advisory seas will
return Sunday morning and afternoon.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, from 11 AM this morning
to 5 PM PDT Sunday. For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 5 PM
this afternoon to 5 AM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Bar crossings will become especially
treacherous.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
properties.instruction:
Recreational boaters should remain in port. Commercial vessels
should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.

properties.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Apache Junction/Gold Canyon, Globe/Miami, Mazatzal
Mountains, Pinal/Superstition Mountains, Rio Verde/Salt River, San
Carlos, and Superior.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger
vehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured
objects may become airborne. Localized channels of blowing dust may
briefly lower visibility under one mile.
properties.instruction:
A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40
mph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this
strong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles.

In addition, strong winds over desert areas could result in briefly
lowered visibilities to well under a mile at times in blowing dust or
blowing sand. Use extra caution.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THIS MORNING TO 7 PM
CDT THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND SHIFT, MOISTURE DROP AND WIND, LOW
RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF NORTH CENTRAL AND NORTHWEST
LOUISIANA...

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of north central and northwest Louisiana.

* TIMING...From 9 AM this morning to 7 PM CDT this evening.

* WINDS...Northeast winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 31 to 69 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 17 at 3:35AM EDT until October 20 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves
of 8 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected
in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from
2 PM this afternoon to 8 AM EDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 5 PM this afternoon to 8 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore currents will
